title: Draft: pcapng: Byte-swap the Darwin packet options when the section needs it
description:
Fixes the big-endian test failures John Thacker reported on !26479 (the s390x Ubuntu build).

The Darwin per-packet options (`OPT_PKT_DARWIN_*`: the process information block references, service class, metadata flags, flow ID, drop reason and line, compression generation count, trace tag) were copied out of the file as they are, with the handlers ignoring their `byte_swapped` argument, since the Darwin metadata support was added in 389f6356c9. A file whose section byte order differs from the host's therefore read them wrong, e.g. a block reference of 1 became 16777216 on a big-endian host reading Apple's tcpdump output, so the process it named was not found. The 16-bit options were also read as 32 bits, taking in the padding. The tests added in !26479 (the first ones to look up a Darwin block other than the first) exposed it.

This swaps them like the standard options, reads the 16-bit ones as 16 bits, and adds a big-endian copy of the Darwin test capture (from the same generator), running the three Darwin tests on both, so a host of either byte order exercises the swapped path. The little-endian file passes on big-endian hosts for the same reason the big-endian one now passes here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01MeQMmftoMWrDyC8HdFk7sT

notes.body:
@oesh, I don't remember whether it was determined whether the fields in the Darwin options should always be treated as little-endian, given that support for them was added after Apple stopped supporting PowerPC processors and I doubt Apple plans to switch back to the Power ISA, and I also doubt Apple are likely to port macOS to z/Architecture or SPARC (much less the Motorola 68k family, which they dropped even before switching to Mac OS X).

Does any Apple software, whether it's publicly available or not, assume that the multi-byte integral fields in any of the Apple-added blocks or options, are little-endian regardless of the byte order in the Section Header Block? If so, we should probably decree that all of those fields are little-endian regardless of the byte order of the SHB for the section they're in.

Either answer needs a change from what's in master today, which reads the per-packet Darwin options without any swapping and so gets them wrong on a big-endian host even for Apple's own little-endian files. This MR implements the section-byte-order reading, which is how the Darwin process information block body is already read (its process ID and options are swapped with the section). If the decision is that Apple's blocks and options are little-endian regardless of the SHB, as the Wireshark custom block already specifies for its entries, I'll switch both the block body and the options to fixed little-endian (swap on big-endian hosts only) and regenerate the big-endian test file with little-endian Darwin values inside the big-endian section; the test would then check exactly that rule. For real Apple files the two readings agree, since the sections are little-endian, so the s390x failure is fixed either way.
let me double check and get back to you.
No BE ISA in foreseeable future. Darwin options are always LE.
